 Judgment

This is an appeal filed by the claimants seeking enhancement of the compensation, aggrieved by the award passed in MVC No.1673/2016, dated 09.01.2018, by the Senior Civil Judge And MACT at Kalaiah vs Jalendra.

2 Arkalgud.
2.
The claim petition is filed seeking compensation of Rs.15,00,000/- for the death of the deceased in the accident that took place on 23.04.2016.

The case of the claimants is that the deceased and others were sitting near a road and a lorry driven by its driver in rash and negligent manner dashed against the deceased causing the accident, she sustained injuries and immediately she was shifted to the hospital and later she succumbed to the said injuries.
According to the claimants the deceased was working as a coolie and earning an amount of Rs.10,000/- p.m.

The court below had taken the monthly income at Rs.4,000/- p.m., and deducted 1/4th towards personal income, which comes to Rs.3,000/- and by applying the NC: 2023:KHC:40770 multiplier granted an amount of Rs.3,24,000/- towards loss of dependency.
Towards funeral expenses, cremation, loss of love and affection, loss of estate, loss of consortium Rs.15,000/- was awarded, towards medical expenses an amount of Rs.11,100/- was granted.
Altogether an amount of Rs.3,85,100/- was granted.

3. Learned counsel appearing for the claimants submits that the court below ought to have taken the income of the deceased at Rs.10,000/- p.m., instead of that court below had taken Rs.4,000/- which is on lower side.
It is submitted that towards other conventional heads also the amounts that are granted by the court below were not correct and he submits that the compensation granted is not just and reasonable.

4. Learned counsel appearing for the insurance company submits that the court below ought to have considered the case of husband as the only dependent, whereas other four members are the major sons who are NC: 2023:KHC:40770 not independent and no evidence is let in to show that they were depending on her.
But the court below deducted 1/4th towards personal expenses.
5. The learned counsel appearing for the claimant submits that the insurance company has not preferred any appeal and it is an appeal of the claimant.
In their appeal the insurance company cannot raise these kind of grounds and whatever the court below has considered had to be retained.

Learned counsel submits that the court below though has held that the accident had taken place because of the rash and negligent driving of the driver of the lorry, on the ground that the driver of the lorry was not having a driving license to drive a heavy goods vehicle and it amounts to violation of the terms and conditions of the policy held that the owner of the vehicle alone is liable to pay the compensation and not the insurance company.

He submits that even if the driver was not having a valid driving license, the deceased being a third party, the insurance company is liable to pay the compensation and NC: 2023:KHC:40770 recover the same from the owner of the vehicle.

The owner has also preferred MFA No.4253/2019, wherein the Court had passed an order on 02.02.2022 granting time to the owner of the vehicle to deposit the amount and a default order is passed and if the same is not deposited without further reference to the court, the same shall be dismissed for non-prosecution and as he failed to comply with the order, the appeal was dismissed.
6.
Having heard the learned counsel on either side, perused the entire material on record.

In this case first coming to the liability aspect, the Tribunal has exonerated the insurance company on the ground that the driver of the appellant vehicle was not having a driving license to drive the heavy goods vehicle.
As rightly contended by the learned counsel for the appellant, the deceased being a Kalaiah vs Jalendra.

K. H on 15 November, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/116687594/
3 third party, whether there is any violation of the terms and conditions of the policy, still the insurance company is liable to pay and recover the same from the owner.
In view of the same, the insurance NC: 2023:KHC:40770 company is liable to pay the compensation and recover the amount from the owner of the vehicle.
7. Then coming to the compensation, the court below had taken Rs.4,000/- as monthly income of the deceased.
This accident is of the year 2016, considering the year of the accident, this Court is inclined to take an amount of Rs.9,500/- as the income of the deceased.
She was aged 60 years as per post-mortem report, hence no future prospects can be granted.
As rightly pointed out by the learned counsel for the insurance company all the four sons are majors, and there is no evidence to show that they were dependents on the deceased.

Hence, this court is inclined to reduce 50%
towards personal expenses, it comes to Rs.4,750/- and the relevant multiplier is 9.
Therefore, the claimants are entitled for an amount of Rs.5,13,000/- towards loss of dependency.

As there are five claimants four sons and husband towards consortium they are entitled for an amount of NC:
2023:KHC:40770 Rs.2,20,000/- (Rs.44,000 x 5), towards funeral expenses an amount of Rs.33,000/- is granted.
Towards medical expenses court below had granted Rs.11,100/- basing on the medical bills and receipts and this court is not inclined to interfere.

8. In the light of the law laid down by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of V.MEKALA vs. M.
MALATHI AND ANOTHER1, the claimant is entitled for an amount of Rs.10,000/- towards Legal Expenses.

The insurance company shall pay the compensation and recover the same from the owner of the offending vehicle.
